verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev ships an official MCP server that lets external AI assistants/agents call tools to trigger and monitor a user's defined tasks/projects (docs-18, docs-29, probe-4), which does let an external agent invoke user workflows via MCP. However, this is a fixed set of platform-level control tools (list projects, trigger task, monitor runs) rather than each individual workflow/connected-app action being dynamically surfaced as its own named MCP tool, and there's no evidence of exposing third-party 'connected app' actions specifically. Missing for 10: per-workflow dynamic tool generation, exposing connected third-party app actions as distinct MCP tools, and independent/hands-on confirmation of external agents successfully calling arbitrary user workflows through the server.
